content.title: Former Kansas City Royals outfielder Terrance Gore dies at 34
content.text: IE 11 is not supported. For an optimal experience visit our site on another browser.Skip to ContentTerrance Gore in Arlington, Texas, in 2020.Kelly Gavin / MLB Photos via Getty Images fileShareAdd NBC News to GoogleSavewith a NBCUniversal ProfileFeb. 7, 2026, 3:31 PM CSTBy Mirna Alsharif and Emilie DornFormer Kansas City Royals outfielder and World Series winner Terrance Gore has died at the age of 34, according to Major League Baseball.Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.Gore played for the Kansas City Royals when they won the American League Championship Series back to back in 2014 and 2015, as well as the 2015 World Series.“We are heartbroken from the loss of Terrance Gore, and send our love to his family and loved ones,” the Kansas City Royals said in a statement.The circumstances surrounding Gore’s death are not clear at this time.In a statement, MLB said it was “shocked and saddened” to learn of Gore’s death. The league remembered the former player as a “speedy outfielder and pinch-running specialist” who stole 43 bases over his regular-season career and was caught only nine times.RecommendedU.S. newsU.S. newsRemains of 3 children were likely in a wooded area 'for several years' before discovery, Memphis police sayU.S. newsU.S. newsMissing doctoral students were romantically linked, would never vanish willingly, family says“He was 5-for-6 in Postseason stolen base attempts and stole 324 bases in 11 Minor League seasons,” MLB said.Gore played eight major-league seasons from 2014 to 2022, landing stints at the Chicago Cubs, Los Angeles Dodgers, Atlanta Braves and the New York Mets.The Dodgers on Saturday also expressed their sorrow over Gore’s death.ShareAdd NBC News to GoogleSavewith a
